research_objects.summary: Bounded Sunshine Machine / PCE pass on persistence versus foregrounding.
Bryan P. Sanders, Class Never Ends (2018).
George Siemens, Connectivism: A Learning Theory for the Digital Age (2005).
Persistence and foregrounding are distinct governance acts; quiet continuity keeps traces returnable without compulsory salience.
Selective Attention and Initiative Authority provide current design analogues without constituting learner-effect evidence.
What may a PCE legitimately keep in the background, for how long, and under whose authority?

ctc_tags.rationale: Learner authority over what returns to the foreground remains central.

ctc_tags.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_tags.rationale: Persistent traces can remain material for later inquiry without dictating the next move.
Return to preserved traces can support later reinterpretation.
Networked traces and weak ties can expand possible connections while preserving source distinction.

ontology_tags.rationale: Foregrounding authority affects learner attention and initiative.
Repeated machine-selected salience can quietly narrow future trajectories.
Maintained connections, external knowledge, and weak ties pressure the PCE account.
Human and machine participation can recursively alter what becomes available for later inquiry.
Background persistence can preserve possibilities without forcing immediate selection.

uncaptured_observations: Retention authority may need to remain distinct from resurfacing authority.
Quiet continuity needs a privacy and forgetting boundary before it can become a stronger design principle.
Weak-tie protection may matter if relevance compounding repeatedly favors already-salient traces.
